title: Dont, de qui et duquel
summary: Express `de`-complements, possession and subsets without losing a compound preposition or duplicating possession.
objectives: Use `dont` for a simple `de` relationship, possession and an included subset.
Choose `de qui` for people and `duquel` forms where an entire compound preposition must remain.

sources.label: Académie française: dont, full and shortened subset clauses and manner
Larousse: relative qui and prepositional person references

sections.title: `Dont` incorporates a simple `de` relationship
paragraphs: `Dont` is a relative pronoun that normally replaces a complement introduced by simple `de`: `parler de`, `avoir besoin de`, `être fier de`. It can refer to people or things and does not change for gender or number. Do not repeat `de` or `en` for the same role.

For a person, `de qui` is a legitimate alternative in appropriate `de`-complement clauses: `la personne de qui je parle`. `Duquel/de laquelle/desquels/desquelles` may also occur, especially in formal style or for clarity; with a plain verb + `de`, `dont` is generally lighter and more idiomatic. This does not mean `duquel` can replace every `dont`: possessive and subset constructions have their own structure.
points: `Duquel` = `de` + `lequel`; `de laquelle` does not contract; `desquels/desquelles` are plural contractions.

examples.french: Le document **dont** j'ai besoin est signé.
examples.english: The document I need is signed.

examples.french: La personne **de qui** je parle habite ici.
examples.english: The person I am talking about lives here.
examples.note: `Dont` is also natural for this person.

examples.french: Les résultats **dont** elle est fière sont publics.
examples.english: The results she is proud of are public.

examples.french: Le financement **duquel** dépend la rénovation n'est pas garanti.
examples.english: The funding on which the renovation depends is not guaranteed.
examples.note: A formal inflected `de`-relative with a thing; `dont` would be a lighter alternative.

mistakes.avoid: Le dossier dont j'en ai besoin est ici.
mistakes.prefer: Le dossier dont j'ai besoin est ici.
mistakes.why: `Dont` already represents the `de`-complement; `en` duplicates the same role.

sections.title: Whose uses `dont` plus an ordinary article
paragraphs: For possession, `dont` links a possessor to a noun inside the relative clause: `une artiste dont le frère est musicien`. The possessive relationship is already expressed by `dont`, so use `le/la/les` or another appropriate nonredundant determiner, not `son/sa/ses` for that same possessor.

The owned noun can be the subject or object of the relative clause: `dont le livre a paru` / `dont j'ai lu le livre`. Keep normal subject-verb order; `dont` is not itself the subject of a verb whose subject is `le livre`. Possession can be a broad relationship, not literal ownership.

examples.french: J'ai rencontré une traductrice **dont la sœur** vit à Dakar.
examples.english: I met a translator whose sister lives in Dakar.

examples.french: Voici le chercheur **dont j'ai lu les articles**.
examples.english: Here is the researcher whose articles I have read.
examples.note: `Les articles` is the object after `lu`; do not force a whose + noun word order.

examples.french: La maison **dont le toit** a été réparé est à vendre.
examples.english: The house whose roof has been repaired is for sale.
examples.note: `Dont` can express a part-whole relationship with a thing.

mistakes.avoid: L'autrice dont son roman a reçu un prix est ici.
mistakes.prefer: L'autrice dont le roman a reçu un prix est ici.
mistakes.why: `Dont` already identifies the possessor; `son` redundantly repeats that relationship.

sections.title: Including and a quantity of which
paragraphs: `Dont` can introduce a subset of a previously mentioned group, often in a shortened clause: `dix participants, dont trois débutants` = ten participants, including three beginners. It can also introduce a full clause with a quantity: `trois de ces livres sont traduits` → `des livres dont trois sont traduits`.

The number after `dont` belongs inside the total, not in addition to it. If six people attend, `dont deux médecins` means six in total, including two doctors. A full clause's verb agrees with its own subject, such as `deux`, not with the whole antecedent.

examples.french: Nous avons reçu douze demandes, **dont quatre** urgentes.
examples.english: We received twelve requests, including four urgent ones.

examples.french: Il apporte cinq livres, **dont deux sont** illustrés.
examples.english: He is bringing five books, two of which are illustrated.

sections.title: Décrire les éléments d'un sous-ensemble
paragraphs: A subset can itself be followed by a relative clause. Compare `dont deux sont disponibles`, where `deux` directly serves as the subject of `sont`, with `dont deux qui sont disponibles`, where `qui` introduces a further description of those two. A finite verb after `dont` does not automatically require an extra `qui` or `que`.

When you do add a relative after the subset, its grammatical role determines `qui` or `que`. `Dont deux que nous utilisons` has `nous` as subject and `que` as the object used. `Dont deux qui fonctionnent` has `qui` as subject. With `avoir`, an object `que` before the participle can trigger agreement with the subset's understood noun, just as in an ordinary relative clause.

examples.french: Le centre possède neuf appareils, **dont deux sont** inutilisables.
examples.english: The centre owns nine devices, two of which are unusable.
examples.note: A full clause already has its subject `deux`; no extra relative is required.

examples.french: Le centre possède neuf appareils, **dont deux qui fonctionnent** sans électricité.
examples.english: The centre owns nine devices, including two that work without electricity.
examples.note: `Qui` begins a description of two devices.

examples.french: Nous avons comparé six méthodes, **dont deux que** l'équipe **avait déjà testées**.
examples.english: We compared six methods, including two that the team had already tested.
examples.note: `Que` is the preceding direct object, referring to two feminine `méthodes`; `testées` agrees.

mistakes.avoid: Il propose trois solutions, dont une que fonctionne sans réseau.
mistakes.prefer: Il propose trois solutions, dont une qui fonctionne sans réseau.
mistakes.why: The further relative needs a subject for `fonctionne`, so use `qui`. `Dont une fonctionne sans réseau` is also grammatical.

sections.title: Préciser de qui ou de quoi on parle
paragraphs: An inflected relative can sometimes distinguish two possible antecedents. In a phrase mentioning a woman and a masculine institution, `de laquelle` points to the woman while `duquel` points to the institution. `Dont` cannot provide that gender signal. Inflection is not a cure for every ambiguity: if both antecedents have the same gender and number, repeat the name or split the sentence.

`La façon dont` and `la manière dont` mean the way in which. Here `dont` expresses a manner relationship, not ownership or an included subset. Use a complete clause after it without repeating a word for that same relationship. With compound prepositions, people can be plural too: `à côté de qui` does not become invalid because it refers to several colleagues.
points: `La façon` (f.) and `la manière` (f.) mean a way or manner; choose `dont` in the pattern taught here.

examples.french: Je connais la directrice du musée, **de laquelle** vous m'avez parlé.
examples.english: I know the director of the museum, about whom you told me.
examples.note: `De laquelle` points to the woman, not to masculine `musée`. With `dont`, the intended referent would depend more on context.

examples.french: La directrice du musée **duquel** dépend cette annexe nous recevra.
examples.english: The director of the museum on which this annex depends will receive us.

examples.french: J'apprécie **la manière dont** vous présentez les limites du projet.
examples.english: I appreciate the way you present the project's limitations.
examples.note: `Dont` relates to a manner, not an owner.

examples.french: Les bénévoles **à côté de qui** nous travaillons connaissent bien le matériel.
examples.english: The volunteers beside whom we work know the equipment well.
examples.note: `De qui` is invariable and can refer to several people; `à côté desquels` is also possible.

sections.title: Do not cut a compound preposition in half
paragraphs: A compound preposition is a multiword relation, such as `près de` (near), `à côté de` (beside), `au sujet de` (about), `à cause de` (because of), `au bord de` (at the edge of). Keep the whole expression when adding a relative: `près duquel, près de laquelle, près desquels, près desquelles`. `Dont` cannot simply replace the final `de` while leaving a stranded `près` or `à côté`.

With people, preposition + `de qui` is also possible: `à côté de qui`. For things, use agreeing `duquel` forms. This is the crucial contrast with simple `parler de`: `le sujet dont nous parlons` but `le sujet au sujet duquel nous échangeons des messages`. Prefer a simpler expression if it communicates the same relationship clearly.

examples.french: Le canal **au bord duquel** nous marchons est calme.
examples.english: The canal along which we are walking is quiet.

examples.french: Les écoles **près desquelles** nous habitons sont petites.
examples.english: The schools near which we live are small.

examples.french: La collègue **à côté de qui** je suis assis prend des notes.
examples.english: The colleague beside whom I am sitting is taking notes.
examples.note: For a woman, `à côté de laquelle` is also grammatical.

practice.prompt: Supply qui or que after the subset: Il reste sept propositions, dont trois ___ le jury souhaite examiner.
practice.explanation: Le jury is the subject; que supplies examiner's object.

practice.prompt: Supply qui or que: Le catalogue comporte dix modèles, dont quatre ___ résistent au gel.
practice.explanation: The further relative needs a subject for résistent.

practice.prompt: Supply only vérifier's participle: La liste contient huit adresses, dont deux que nous avons déjà ___.
practice.explanation: Que refers to two feminine plural addresses and precedes avoir + participle.

practice.prompt: Is an extra qui required in Nous avons recruté cinq guides, dont deux parlent arabe?
choices: No; deux is already the subject of parlent.
Yes; every finite verb after dont needs a second relative pronoun.
answers: No; deux is already the subject of parlent.
practice.explanation: A subset can be the subject of its own full clause without an additional relative.

practice.prompt: Refer explicitly to the woman, not the masculine committee, using an inflected de-relative: La présidente du comité, ___ vous parlez, sera présente.
practice.explanation: Feminine singular de laquelle selects présidente; dont would not carry that gender signal.

practice.prompt: Use dont to link a manner: La façon ___ les dossiers sont classés facilite la recherche.
practice.explanation: La façon dont introduces how something is done, not a possession.

practice.prompt: Use an inflected de-relative referring to masculine service: La responsable du service ___ dépend cette unité est absente.
practice.explanation: Dépendre de supplies de; duquel identifies service rather than feminine responsable.

practice.prompt: Complete for several male colleagues, retaining à côté: Les collègues à côté ___ je suis installé parlent espagnol.
practice.explanation: Invariable de qui works for plural people; the agreeing contraction desquels is another valid answer.

practice.prompt: Supply the single de-relative in this manner expression: Nous discuterons de la manière ___ l'accueil est organisé.
practice.explanation: La manière dont expresses the way in which reception is organized.

practice.prompt: Two masculine singular committees could be meant. Will duquel by itself distinguish them?
choices: No; repeat the intended committee's name or restructure.
Yes; an inflected relative always removes ambiguity.
answers: No; repeat the intended committee's name or restructure.
practice.explanation: Gender and number only help when the competing antecedents differ.

practice.prompt: Supply the single uninflected relative: Les outils ___ nous avons besoin sont chers.
practice.explanation: Avoir besoin de takes a de-complement.

practice.prompt: Supply only the relative meaning whose: La femme ___ le fils travaille ici arrive demain.
practice.explanation: Dont links the woman to her son; le is already provided.

practice.prompt: Supply the relative meaning including: Huit invités, ___ deux journalistes, sont présents.
practice.explanation: The journalists form a subset of the eight guests.

practice.prompt: Supply the full phrase 'near which' with près and a masculine singular antecedent: Le lac ___ nous campons.
practice.explanation: Keep près de and contract de + lequel.

practice.prompt: Supply the single uninflected relative: La décision ___ elle est fière a changé sa vie.
practice.explanation: Fier de supplies the relationship.

practice.prompt: Use de + qui to refer to the person: Le témoin ___ nous parlons est absent. Supply both words.
practice.explanation: De qui is legitimate for a person; the prompt specifies this alternative.

practice.prompt: Supply the definite article, not a possessive: Les voisins dont ___ fille est médecin déménagent.
practice.explanation: Dont already supplies the parental relationship.

practice.prompt: Complete with the de-relative after à côté: La maison à côté ___ nous attendons est bleue.
practice.explanation: Feminine singular de laquelle does not contract.

practice.prompt: Complete with the de-relative: Les bâtiments près ___ vous travaillez sont récents.
practice.explanation: Masculine plural: de + lesquels.

practice.prompt: Complete with the de-relative: Les routes au bord ___ poussent ces arbres sont étroites.
practice.explanation: Feminine plural after the complete phrase au bord de.

practice.prompt: Supply être in the present: Elle propose quatre dates, dont deux ___ possibles.
practice.explanation: Deux is the plural subject of the relative clause.

practice.prompt: Dix bénévoles, dont trois étudiants: how many volunteers in total?
practice.explanation: Dont includes a subset within the total.

practice.prompt: Use an inflected de + lequel form, not dont: Le budget ___ dépend ce projet reste incertain.
practice.explanation: Dépendre de with masculine singular budget permits formal duquel; dont is normally lighter but the prompt explicitly requests the inflected form.

practice.prompt: Supply the single relative: Voici l'écrivaine ___ j'ai acheté le dernier roman.
practice.explanation: The novel belongs to the writer; its object position after acheté is normal.

practice.prompt: Remove only the redundant pronoun: Le problème dont j'en parle est sérieux. Supply the corrected full sentence.
answers: Le problème dont je parle est sérieux.
practice.explanation: Dont and en cannot duplicate this de-complement.

practice.prompt: Complete for a female colleague: La collègue à côté ___ je travaille est patiente.
practice.explanation: Both forms work for a person after the full compound preposition.

practice.prompt: Supply the relative for a subset: Six dossiers sont complets, ___ un très détaillé.
practice.explanation: One detailed file is included among the six.

production_task.prompt: Describe a small association: a person whose work matters, a resource it needs, the building near which it meets, and a numerical subset of members.
production_task.model_answer: Notre présidente, dont les conseils sont précieux, connaît bien le quartier. Le matériel dont nous avons besoin est simple. Nous nous réunissons près d'une école, à côté de laquelle se trouve un jardin. Nous sommes quinze membres, dont quatre retraités.
production_task.translation: Our chair, whose advice is valuable, knows the neighbourhood well. The equipment we need is simple. We meet near a school, beside which there is a garden. We are fifteen members, including four retirees.
rubric: `Dont` expresses possession without a redundant possessive.
The simple `de`-complement is not repeated with `en`.
The subset belongs within the stated total.
